insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Base Sum Insured options: 3L, 4L, 5L, 7.5L, 10L, 12.5L, 15L, 20L, 25L, 50L, 75L, 100L (Individual/Family Floater); Total SI may include Booster Benefit and optional Safeguard/Safeguard+; plus ReAssure benefit

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: ReAssure Unlimited reinstatement up to base Sum Insured. (Applicable for both same & different illness)
great.explanation: Unlimited reinstatement is available up to the base Sum Insured, and it applies for both same and different illnesses. This greatly improves protection if you need multiple hospitalizations in the same policy year.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The sequence of utilization of Sum Insured will be as below: i. Base Sum Insured ... iii. Accumulated Cumulative Bonus under Booster benefit (if any) followed by; iv. ReAssure benefit
great.explanation: After the Base Sum Insured (and any accumulated Cumulative Bonus under Booster, if available) is used, the ReAssure benefit is utilized. This effectively gives an additional insurer-funded cover layer once the base cover is exhausted.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy .
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This is within common market ranges for retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This is a standard waiting period seen in many plans.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy commencement, except accidents. This is the usual initial waiting period structure in India.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will pay above mentioned Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for period up to 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days immediately before admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for up to 180 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days immediately after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment costs for up to 6 months.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote:
Annexure II - The expenses that are not covered or subsumed into room charges / procedure charges / costs of treatment
List  I – Expenses not covered ... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ...
bad.reference: Annexure II (List I – Expenses not covered)
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves, masks, and nebulisation kits are listed as not covered. This can increase out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization because hospitals commonly bill these separately.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment (if applicable) as specified in the Policy Schedule shall be applicable on the amount payable by Us.
bad.explanation: A co-payment can apply as per the Policy Schedule on the amount payable by the insurer. If co-pay is present in your schedule, you will have to bear that percentage of every admissible claim.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: Room Rent means the amount charged by a Hospital towards Room and Boarding expenses and shall include the associated medical expenses.
unclear.reference: Section 3.1.41 (Room Rent) + Annexure I (Inpatient Care: 'Covered up to Sum Insured')
unclear.explanation: The wording shown only defines room rent and does not clearly state any eligible room category or cap in the quoted text. If a room rent limit exists in the Policy Schedule, choosing a higher room can lead to reduced claim payments via linked deductions.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
